title: Bit-depth Econ Calibrator — Heuristic Workbook
content:
Purpose:
This workbook captures a compact, heuristic-first approach to calibrating cost/latency/quality tradeoffs across bit depths (4-bit, INT8, FP8) for inference workloads. The goal is to produce a small, auditable rule-set that teams can drop into an experiment spreadsheet and get immediate deployment guidance (recommended bit-depth, expected per-token cost delta, latency impact, and guardrail checks).

When to use this: quick spikes, baseline recommendations for new models, and serving-policy fallbacks where we need a simple decision rule rather than a full retraining/eval pipeline. Not a replacement for full evals but intended to reduce iteration time for SRE/SE/ML engineers.

Key assumptions (editable at top of sheet):
- baseline_model = full-precision FP16 throughput/loss metrics must be present (tokens/sec, baseline_quality_score).
- workload profile: median_seq_len, p95_seq_len, requests_per_sec and steady-state concurrency.
- hardware profile: GPU type + effective_fp8_kernels flag (gpu_sku).
- cost inputs: gpu_hour_price_usd, infra_overhead_percent (network, orchestration).
- quality decay modeled as additive delta in end-metric (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE/F1/QA-EM) per bit-step.

Spreadsheet layout (recommended tabs):
1_meta — editable knobs, definitions, and quick hazard checks.
2_latency_profiles — measured baseline latencies by seq_len percentiles and simple scaling transform for lower bitwidths.
3_cost_curves — token throughput estimates and derived cost per 1k tokens for each bit-depth & quant method.
4_quality_fit — small dataset of quality deltas by quantization mode, fitted with a 1- or 2- parameter exponential decay: quality(bit) = baseline_quality - A * exp(-B * bits_equiv).
5_decision_grid — combinatorial table mapping (SLO x cost-sensitivity x quality-threshold) to recommended bit-depth.
6_scenarios — templated rows for canary/production scenarios, including rollout steps, margin of safety, and fallback model IDs.
7_results — experiment outputs, logs, and final recommended policy snippet for the Console rollout config.

Core heuristic formulas (put these in simple cells):
- throughput_tokens_per_sec(bit, gpu) = baseline_tps * speedup_factor(bit, gpu)
  where speedup_factor ~ 1 + alpha_gpu * (baseline_bits - target_bits)
  (alpha_gpu: empirical per-GPU kernel speedup coefficient; default 0.18 for Ampere-class with INT8 kernels, 0.28 if optimized FP8 kernels available)

- latency_p50(bit) = latency_p50_baseline / speedup_factor(bit) + sequence_penalty
  sequence_penalty = p95_seq_len_ratio * 0.003 * (p95_seq_len - median_seq_len) 

- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd = (gpu_hour_price_usd / (throughput_tokens_per_sec * 3600)) * 1000 * (1 + infra_overhead_percent)

- expected_quality_score = baseline_quality - quality_delta(bit, model_family)
  quality_delta heuristics (default):
    4-bit (mixed) => 0.10 - 0.20 relative metric drop (depends on LM family and task sensitivity)
    INT8 (w/ calibration) => 0.04 - 0.10
    FP8 (w/ kernel support) => 0.02 - 0.06
  Workflows must replace these with fitted values from tab 4_quality_fit.

Decision rule (one-line):
If SLO_latency_target is strict (p50_target < baseline_p50 * 0.85) -> prefer FP8 or INT8 where kernels are supported; else if cost-target is < baseline_cost * 0.55 -> consider mixed 4-bit with allowed quality_margin >= 0.12.

Compact utility: bit-depth ladder selector (to implement as sheet formulas or a single helper cell):
- Input knobs: quality_threshold_delta (how much quality you can lose), cost_budget_pct (relative to baseline), latency_slo_multiplier (relative to baseline p50)
- Evaluate each candidate (4-bit, INT8, FP8): compute expected_quality_score, cost_per_1k, latency_p50.
- Score candidate: score = w_q * normalized_quality + w_c * normalized_cost + w_l * normalized_latency (weights editable). Choose max score.

Example scenario rows (copy into 6_scenarios):
- Search-typo-correction: median_seq=32, p95=128, rps=80, baseline_p50=46ms, baseline_quality=0.92.
  - INT8 recommended: est_cost_delta -38%, est_latency_p50 -22%, expected_quality 0.88 -> run 2% A/B to monitor answer fidelity and hallucination metric for top-10.
- Long-instruction-qa: median_seq=256, p95=1024, rps=3, baseline_p50=280ms, baseline_quality=0.95.
  - FP8 recommended if hardware has optimized kernels (est_cost_delta -27%, latency -18%, quality 0.94). 4-bit shows larger quality loss; schedule offline eval.

Experiment checklist (for engineers copy-paste):
- Small-scale baseline collection: collect p50/p95 latencies at target concurrency for FP16 baseline.
- Fit quality decay on a 500-sample holdout with representative prompts (tab 4_quality_fit).
- Run the throughput microbench on identical hardware (tab 2_latency_profiles).
- Populate cost inputs and compute cost_per_1k in 3_cost_curves.
- Canary plan: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% with rollback thresholds on hallucination rate and latency SLO breaches.

Rollout policy snippet (console-ready, fill values from sheet):
- model_variant: redwood-model-vX-4bit-mixed
- rollout: canary -> linear-step (1% for 24h -> 10% for 48h -> scale)
- fallback: model_variant: redwood-model-vX-int8-calibrated if hallucination_rate > threshold or latency_slo_breaches > 2/day

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate alpha_gpu defaults across latest GPU fleet (A100, H100, L4). Current values are placeholders.
- Add small script to auto-scrape Console per-route token breakdown to seed throughput_inputs.
- Formalize quality_delta estimation pipeline (link to JIRA-OPT-412).

Notes & provenance:
- Heuristics here were distilled from 9 internal quant experiments run across mid-2024 to 2025 (summary in linked PR).
- This sheet is intentionally conservative on quality; teams can loosen thresholds after full evals.

Quick bookmarks (paste these into sheet header):
- How to use: edit 1_meta > Set baseline metrics > fill tabs 2-4 > review 5_decision_grid > copy final policy into 7_results
- Safety guard: if expected_quality_score < baseline_quality - 0.15, mark candidate as "unsafe" and require offline eval.

Contact: Maya Chen (owner) — mention in #optimize or DM for quick reviews.

Appendix (short formula cheat sheet):
- cost_per_1k = round((gpu_price / (baseline_tps * speedup * 3600)) * 1000 * (1 + overhead), 5)
- speedup_factor_estimates: 4-bit: 1.4x-2.0x (high variance), INT8: 1.15x-1.5x, FP8: 1.10x-1.4x
- quality_delta default table: [model_family: {4bit: 0.12, int8: 0.07, fp8: 0.035}] (replace with fit)

End of workbook notes.

-- Maya
